full_judgment:
7. The Mill authorities sent a three-member Committee to Kanaipur Centre to make preliminary enquiry as to whether the jute in question was purchased and dispatched by trucks from Kanaipur. On consideration of the report of this Committee the higher authorities suspected foul play in the matter. So they constituted a regular Committee of Enquiry consisting of two high officials of the BJMC. This Committee held enquiry from 4 to 6 April 1988 against the appellant and many others including the Deputy Manager, Delwar Hossain. The enquiry was held in presence of the appellant and about a dozen officers and employees connected with jute purchase matters. The Committee examined all connected papers, documents and registers at different places including Kamarkhali Ferryghat and submitted its report which included a finding to this effect: The jute was not purchased at Kanaipur nor was it sent from there. by truck to Khulna, that the jute was purchased from Jhikargacha, that the truck drivers who could not produce any Ferry-ghat Receipt at the time of interception by the Anti-Corruption, produced five forged/false receipts later on, that there was interpolation in the Ferry-ghat Register, and corresponding interpolation in the Challan Register maintained at Kanaipur Centre, and made observation that so far as the Manager (appellant) is concerned, he had either connived at this purchase or neglected his duty to make independent verification of the questioned jute before he stored it in the godown. 

 8. The BJMC accepted this report and served a second show-cause notice, Annexure-I dated 26-6-89, asking the appellant to show cause why he should not be held guilty and punished by demotion. He gave explanation to the show-cause notice and was also heard in person by the Chairman himself. As appears, the appellant did not deny the foul play found by the Committee but he said that he had no knowledge whatever as to how the jute was purchased or how the interpolations occurred or forged receipts were issued. On these materials the authorities came to the conclusion that the appellant is also responsible for the loss caused to the Mills. As to the Deputy Manager, who was Agency-in-Charge at Kanaipur, he was dismissed from service and about seven other employees were also found guilty and given minor punishment.
